items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I learned that from talking with guys like Bill Holman and Larry Wilcox and you name it, and Mancini.

ctx.x: How do you — what was your entrance like into that world? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

Well Buddy Rich of course put me on the map. You know I played trumpet on Buddy’s band for about four months. He fired me a couple of times, at least a couple of times. But I learned a lot on that band. Of course playing in bands, like with my parents with our family band, you understand how things work. You hear the melody then you hear the counter line. And when I was playing in college, when I played in big bands in college, I had my own big band in Potsdam. Well you get to hear all those inner voicings and…
Well I wondered how you, like if there was a real door that opened you, for your composing and I think you said Buddy Rich because you came back and started writing for him, is that correct?
